slides.name: 2007, the first bus
slides.h: Meet Chuck Cassady (you probably already know him but say hi anyway). A long time ago he bought a transit bus with little idea how to drive it.
slides.sub: The next day, sixteen strangers piled in and drove to Tennessee.

slides.name: He moved into it
slides.h: Chuck was a philosophy student and paying rent was not really his thing. After starting a party-bus company he had an idea.
slides.sub: A couple weeks later he moved into his bus.

slides.name: A home so cozy
slides.h: He ended up building a home so cozy his mom encouraged him to apply to be on a Tiny Home TV Show (moms rock).
slides.sub: He sent in what he calls a cheeky application.

slides.name: A tiny house show
slides.h: They picked him, partly because nobody else on the show was converting a school bus. Some might call Chuck a pioneer but he’s always known he stands on the shoulders of the legends who came before him.

slides.name: 2018 to 2023, the company
slides.h: Building one bus for television turned into building them for everybody else too, and his company Chrome Yellow Corp went on to build about 40 conversions.

slides.name: Two hundred videos
slides.h: Knowing he wouldn’t build forever he started a Youtube channel to pass on his knowledge and filmed over 200 videos and livestreams.
slides.sub: I’ve heard a dozen people say they built their bus “the Chuck Cassady way”.

slides.name: A decade for other people
slides.h: Ten years of finishing other people’s buses was fulfilling, he says, but it kept pulling him away from the part he actually likes.

slides.name: 2021, one for himself
slides.h: He bought a dog-nose short bus with the legendary DT466 (a big boy engine) and started to build a home he could travel in.

slides.name: Inside Oblio
slides.h: Eventually, Chuck completed his masterpiece. His advice? “Don’t worry about the money so much. You’re never going to have enough of it.”
slides.sub: Four years of weekends and about $60,000 in materials later.

slides.name: Oblio finished
slides.h: Now Chuck travels in his rig and helps people finish theirs on site. For the full tour check out our Youtube channel and subscribe for more!

caption:
Chuck Cassady spent about a decade building other people's buses. Oblio is the
first one he had the time to build for himself.

It started in 2007 with a Craigslist ad and a ride to a festival. He was a
philosophy student who wasn't into paying rent, so he moved into the bus. Seven
years and three buses later he decided to do one properly, a tiny house show
picked him, and people started asking him to build theirs. That turned into a
conversion company, two hundred videos teaching other people how, and enough
builds that they call it the Chuck Cassady way.

The catch is that finishing buses for other people kept him away from the part
he likes most, which is travelling.

He bought Oblio in 2021. A 1996 International, 27 and a half feet, twelve inch
roof raise, four years of weekends and about $60,000 in materials.

Full tour is on the channel. The written story is here:
https://mobiledwellings.media/stories/chuck-cassady-oblio
